review.notes: All 25 physical pages' extracted text was swept with 5-gram shingle comparison against the OCR markdown (normalized: math spanned to placeholders, hyphenated line breaks joined); no code fences exist and the heading tree (sections 1-5, appendices A-E) is complete. Tables 1-2 and 4-6 export as intact HTML tables whose rows and scores were spot-checked against the PDF text. Two page-bottom footnote bodies were transcribed from 140/300-dpi renders (physical pp. 8 and 11) and restored; the ref [20] URL underscore was confirmed on a 300-dpi render of physical p.15. Physical p.12 prints the sentence fragment 'Impact of Decoupling Visual Encoders. e efficacy of ...' in the source itself (verified on a 300-dpi render), so the OCR faithfully matches the print and was left unchanged. Prompt-box Python snippets and in-image captions on physical pp. 13, 23-25 are figure-internal text shown by embedded figures and are not defects; MJHQ/appendix numeric shingle gaps resolved to LaTeX math spans and figure axis ticks.

patches.before: Our framework builds upon an enhanced version $^{1}$ of DeepSeek-LLM (1.3B) [7, 64].
patches.after:
Our framework builds upon an enhanced version $^{1}$ of DeepSeek-LLM (1.3B) [7, 64].

$^{1}$This version, trained on an expanded text corpus compared to the one in Janus [97], has been demonstrated to possess better performance on multiple-choice benchmarks (e.g., MMBench [63] and SEED Bench [46]). Our preliminary experiments suggest that it has minimal impact on the quality of visual generation.
patches.evidence: Rendered physical p.8 footnote band prints: '1 This version, trained on an expanded text corpus compared to the one in Janus [97], has been demonstrated to possess better performance on multiple-choice benchmarks (e.g., MMBench [63] and SEED Bench [46]). Our preliminary experiments suggest that it has minimal impact on the quality of visual generation.' The OCR kept the inline marker $^{1}$ on the DeepSeek-LLM sentence but dropped the footnote body; restored after the sentence that carries the marker.

patches.before: all ablation experiments are performed on $256 \times 256$ resolution images $^{2}$ .
patches.after:
all ablation experiments are performed on $256 \times 256$ resolution images $^{2}$ .

$^{2}$The understanding encoders in the $256 \times 256$-based ablation studies is also SigLIP-Large-Patch/16 which is pre-trained on $256 \times 256$ images.
